data.gender_notes: Elpida is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Elpida was the goddess of hope. She was considered the personification of hope and the promise of future good fortune. In the Bible, Elpida is not a named character, but the name means 'hope' in both Greek and Hebrew. The name Elpida carries the meaning “Hope, Expectation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Elpida usually hope their child will grow to embody hope, expectation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of faith and trust in God's plan.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Elpida total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: אלפידה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלפידה היא שם שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו תקווה. השם קשור למושג התקווה והציפיה לאור וישועה. בתרבות היהודית, התקווה היא אחד מעיקרי האמונה והשם אלפידה משקף ערך זה. השם גם מופיע בברית החדשה וקשור לנושא התקווה הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Ἐλπίδα
in_greek.meaning: Ἐλπίδα ἐστιν ὄνομα σημαίνειν ἐλπίδα καὶ ἀσφάλειαν
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἐλπίδα ὄνομα προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑλληνικὴν λέξιν ἐλπίς, ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει ἐλπίδα καὶ ἀσφάλειαν. Ἐν τῇ Καινῇ Διαθήκη, τὸ ὄνομα Ἐλπίδα συσχετίζεται μετὰ τῆς χριστιανικῆς ἐλπίδος καὶ ἀσφαλείας. Τὸ ὄνομα ἦν δημοφιλὲς ἐν τοῖς πρώτοις χριστιανοῖς καὶ ἐκφράζει τὴν ἐλπίδα τῆς σωτηρίας.

in_latin.name: Elpida
in_latin.meaning: Elpida nomen significat spem et expectationem
in_latin.long_meaning: Elpida nomen habet originem in lingua graeca et significat spem et expectationem. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Elpida erat usitatum et significabat spem christianam et salutem. Nomen Elpida etiam in liturgia et hymnis ecclesiasticis invenitur.

historical_references.reference: Elpida of Thessaly was a Christian martyr who lived during the Roman Empire. She was a member of a wealthy family and was known for her exceptional beauty. When Emperor Diocletian issued an edict ordering the persecution of Christians, Elpida was arrested and subjected to various tortures, including being burned at the stake. However, she miraculously survived. She was then sent to the mines, where she continued to suffer but never wavered in her faith. Eventually, she was beheaded for her refusal to renounce Christianity. Her feast day is celebrated on April 13.

Elpida of Cyprus is a legendary figure in Christian folklore. According to tradition, she was a beautiful and virtuous young woman who lived in Cyprus during the early Christian era. Despite her beauty, she remained a devoted virgin and refused the advances of a local ruler. In retaliation, the ruler ordered her to be buried alive in a cave. However, a dove appeared to her in the cave and kept her comforted and sustained until she was rescued by a group of passing monks. Elpida became a revered figure and her legend spread throughout the Christian world. Her feast day is celebrated on May 4.
